snippets.text: SwiftCart's average cost per delivery rose from 5.00 credits in 2024 to 5.40 credits in 2025. Higher fuel and labour costs were cited in its fictional annual report.
The fictional delivery company SwiftCart completed 1 million deliveries in 2025, up from 800,000 in 2024. Its on-time delivery rate rose from 90% to 92%.
The same 2025 online grocery survey found that 360 of 600 online buyers valued delivery reliability most. The survey did not ask respondents to rank every purchasing factor.

draft_memo.title: SwiftCart Delivery Growth and Costs Analysis
draft_memo.body:
SwiftCart completed 1 million deliveries in 2025, which is an increase of 200,000 deliveries from the 800,000 completed in 2024 [P05]. The on-time delivery rate improved from 90% in 2024 to 92% in 2025 [P05]. The average cost per delivery increased from 5.00 credits in 2024 to 5.40 credits in 2025 [P06]. Higher fuel and labour costs were cited as reasons for this increase in delivery costs [P06]. The growth in deliveries from 2024 to 2025 represents a 25% increase in volume [P05]. The increase in average delivery cost by 8% occurred alongside the rise in delivery volume [P06]. SwiftCart's on-time delivery rate of 92% in 2025 shows an improvement over the previous year [P05]. The total number of deliveries in 2025 reached 1 million, marking a notable achievement for the company [P05]. The average cost per delivery in 2025 was 5.40 credits, which is higher than the previous year's cost [P06].

Interpretation: SwiftCart's delivery volume increased by 25% while the on-time delivery rate improved by 2% from 2024 to 2025.

Limitations: The source does not provide information on customer satisfaction or feedback regarding delivery services. There is no data on the geographical distribution of deliveries or variations in performance across different regions. The report does not specify the exact reasons for the increase in fuel and labour costs. There is no mention of how the cost increase affects customer pricing or demand. The impact of the delivery growth on overall market share is not addressed. The source lacks comparative data with competitors in the delivery sector.
